thread:
harper: FYI procurement picked up Meterly and InvoiceFlow proposals. Quick checklist: invoice detail (per-request vs aggregated), dispute window, and renewal protection. Any initial blockers?

devon: Meterly gives per-call line items and supports S3 ledger pushes with record IDs. InvoiceFlow provides daily aggregates only but claims better discounts at scale.

suzie: We had a past issue with an aggregated vendor where a billing discrepancy took 3 weeks to reconcile. For us, per-request granularity is a big ops win.

mike: Pricing snapshot:
```
Meterly: $0.0009/token, no infra fee, optional reporting addon $250/mo
InvoiceFlow: $0.0007/token, +7% network fee, aggregate daily rows, 12mo min commit
```
Link to spreadsheet (internal): https://redwood-internal/sheets/meterly-invoiceflow-eval

devon: Meterly will accept a cap on renewal increases (<=8%) and a 90-day notice clause. InvoiceFlow pushed back on caps but offered a 3-tier usage guarantee.

harper: Finance ask  can Meterly provide a checksum on S3 exports? We need deterministic ingest for our ledger.

devon: They do MD5 checksums and a sequence token. InvoiceFlow only offers SFTP batch with no checksum.

suzie: Ops trade: InvoiceFlow's cheaper unit price might be offset by 8% network fee + 10-15h/mo reconciliation engineering. Estimate that at ~ $3k/mo in ops cost.

mike: Suggest hybrid: use InvoiceFlow for bulk async jobs and Meterly for low-latency routes. If we go hybrid ask both for per-route pricing and a fallthrough MOA.

finance-bot: Action items recorded: harper to request Meterly checksum + sample S3 export (48h), suzie to model ops cost delta (72h), devon to draft counterterms including <=8% renewal cap (5 business days).

harper: I'll schedule vendor follow-up for Mon 9am PT. Thanks all. :calendar:
